item: One extraction at a time, process-wide: a lock around the whole extract_article call tree, because libxml2 aborted the collector in lxml's document_fromstring under about 50 workers and the cause is not established
summary: The 2026-10-14 SIGABRT (lxml/html/__init__.py:740 <- trafilatura load_html <- bare_extraction <- extract_article, ~50 workers, 1 boot in 7) has no known upstream cause; the evidence is inferred from line numbers (trafilatura 2.3.1, lxml 6.1.3), the one loose match (trafilatura #840) is a release older than that. A process-wide RLock now covers the whole call tree so concurrent use of libxml2 is impossible from the app and every tree is freed inside the lock. Measured on 4 CPUs: unlocked threaded extraction is about 4x SLOWER than locked from 4 threads up, the whole pass is no worse locked (0.51/2.45/3.92 vs 0.51/2.40/3.77 articles/s at 1/8/50 workers, 1.5 s fetch delay). tests/test_extract_lock.py (35 tests, 7/7 module mutants killed) pins serialisation of both paths, release on a raise, re-entrancy, trees freed under the lock and an AST walk that nothing else in src/ reaches libxml2. NOT built: a trafilatura>=2.1.0 floor (proposed, with its registry entry), subprocess isolation (OPEN_QUEUE: only if an abort recurs under the lock).
